requirements.evidence: Configurator checks fit/collisions only; parts are user-chosen 3D-printed plastic with no load rating. Built geometry suggests shelving but no verified strength, waterproofing or safety factor. Cannot claim 50 kg capacity.
Two half-base drawers: drawer:0#-1,0#cut on piece:-1,0,0;half-n and drawer:0#1,1#cut on piece:1,1,0;half-n.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey shelf unit (4 cells base + 4 cells level 1 with solid covers as shelf decks) with two half-base drawers and staged books. Load rating cannot be verified in this system — shape only, not certified strength — so 50 kg requirement is marked unmet with explanation.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your shelf unit with drawers is on the workbench — I'll lay out a sturdy frame that shows the form while noting its real load limits.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: I can't certify 50 kg in this printed system, so I'll craft a shelf-shaped frame with drawers as an appearance model only.
